Basement Coatings

Why Basements in Hardin County Need Special Attention

Kentucky's clay-heavy soil is notorious for retaining water, especially after spring rains and during the thaw cycles of late winter. That moisture doesn't just sit on top of the soil — it migrates upward through concrete slabs via vapor transmission, a process that can cause even well-installed coatings to blister and delaminate if the product and prep aren't matched to the site conditions.

Before we coat any basement floor, we test moisture vapor emission rate (MVER). If the reading is within an acceptable range, we proceed with a moisture-tolerant epoxy system. If it's elevated, we either apply a moisture-mitigation primer first or recommend waterproofing remediation — we won't coat a wet slab and collect our check, only for you to call us in six months with a failing floor.

The result of our process is a basement floor that's sealed against dust, resistant to water vapor, easy to clean with a mop, and attractive enough to serve as a living space, recreation room, workshop, or finished storage area.

Basement Coating Options We Offer

100% Solids Epoxy

Our most popular basement system. Applied in two coats with an optional decorative flake broadcast. Provides excellent adhesion to ground concrete and handles moderate moisture vapor levels.

Polyurea / Polyaspartic

Faster cure than epoxy — walk on it within hours, park on it within a day. Better for high-humidity environments and elevated moisture readings. Slightly higher cost than epoxy.

Solid Color Systems

Clean, single-color finish in light gray, charcoal, tan, or custom shades. Great for workshops, storage, and finished spaces where a uniform look is preferred.

Flake Broadcast Systems

Decorative vinyl flake adds texture, hides minor imperfections, and provides slip resistance — ideal for basement recreation rooms and multi-use spaces.
